JUGEMENT SUR DÉCLARATION
EN

PROLONGATION EN VERTU DE

LOI SUR LA PROTECTION DE
LA JEUNESSE

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

Le Tribunal confirme et motive une décision et
une ordonnance rendues dans l'affaire en titre lors de l'audience tenue le 10
mars 2004.

[
2
]

Conformément à l'article 95 de la Loi sur la
protection de la jeunesse, le Directeur de la protection de la jeunesse
(Directeur) demande la prolongation de l'ordonnance rendue le 21 mars 2003
confiant l'adolescent à sa mère sous réserve de la mise en place de diverses
mesures correctives, dont un suivi social, le tout pour une période de 9 mois.

[
3
]

À l'appui de sa demande, le Directeur allègue
les faits suivants :

–    the child remained in the mother's care;

-     the family continued to actively participate in
the Transition Diversion Program;

-     the child's behaviour was initially reported as
having improved, however, in December 2003, the child's situation deteriorated
more particularly but not restrictively in that :

-     the child started missing school;

-     the child is violating curfews;

-     the child does not inform his mother of his
whereabouts;

-     the child associates with negative peers and
adults;

-     on or around January 16
th
, 2004, the
child threatened his younger brother with a knife;

-     for the said incident, the child spent one night
in a group home for respite;

-     on January 28
th
, 2004, the child did
not attend school, spent the day out and only arrived home past his curfew;

-     upon his arrival, the child was defiant towards
the mother and the former went for respite in a group home;

-     on January 29
th
, 2004, the mother
went into the child's bedroom and found marijuana residue as well as drug
paraphernalia;

-     on February 1
st
, 2004, the mother
confronted the child with regards to respecting written rules, however the
child disagreed with the terms of accounting for his whereabouts and therefore
the mother asked for the child to be placed.

[
4
]

En conséquence, le Directeur recommande au Tribunal
de confier de nouveau l'adolescent à sa mère sous réserve de la mise en place
de diverses mesures correctives, dont un suivi social, le tout pour une période
de six mois.

[
5
]

Le 3 février 2004, à titre de mesures provisoires,
du consentement des parties, le juge Guy Lévesque ordonne l'hébergement
obligatoire de l'adolescent en centre de réadaptation pour une période maximale
de 30 jours.

[
6
]

À l'audience, l'adolescent, par la voix de son
avocat, admet ses troubles de comportement et consent aux mesures recherchées
par le Directeur pour y remédier.

[
7
]

La mère, non assistée d'un avocat, admet les
troubles de comportement de son fils et consent aux mesures.

[
8
]

Elle précise qu'elle a convenu avec son fils que si
des mesures de répit s'imposent, elle le confiera à la grand-mère maternelle
plutôt qu'en centre de réadaptation.

[
9
]

Toutefois, si ces mesures ne parviennent pas à
corriger la situation, elle n'hésitera pas à demander son placement en centre
de réadaptation pour une longue période.

[
10
]

Considering the allegations in support of the
declaration;

[
11
]

Considering the mother's admissions and her
consent to the measures recommended by the Director;

[
12
]

Considering the child's admissions and his
consent to the measures recommended by the Director;

[
13
]

Considering the reports filed;

[
14
]

Considering the interest of the child and the
respect of his rights;

[
15
]

THEREFORE, THE  TRIBUNAL:

[
16
]

GRANTS
the
application;

[
17
]

DECLARES
the
security and development of the child still in danger;

[
18
]

EXTENDS
the
decision rendered on September 19
th
, 2003;

[
19
]

ENTRUSTS
the
child to the care of his mother;

[
20
]

ORDERS
that the
child attend a minimum of four substance abuse education and/or treatment
program sessions;

[
21
]

TAKES

NOTICE

that the child agrees to submit to substance abuse testing should this be
requested by his mother and/or the delegate;

[
22
]

ORDERS
that the
child be submitted to substance abuse testing should this be requested by his
mother and/or the delegate;

[
23
]

TAKES

NOTICE

that the child agrees to attend weekly group family therapy meetings at the
Jewish General Hospital, until completion of the program;

[
24
]

ORDERS
that the
child attend weekly group family therapy meetings at the Jewish General
Hospital, until completion of the program;

[
25
]

ORDERS
that the
child follow the rules at home, at school and in the community;

[
26
]

ORDERS
that the
child refrain from any form of aggression;

[
27
]

ORDERS
that the
child account to his mother for his whereabouts;

[
28
]

RECOMMENDS
that
the family explore respite option within their extended family network, to use
as needed and with the consent of all parties;

[
29
]

ORDERS
that a
person working for Ville Marie Child and Youth Protection Centre provide aid,
counsel and assistance to the child and the family;

[
30
]

THE WHOLE
for a
period of 6 months;

[
31
]

ENTRUSTS
the situation
of the child to the Director of Youth Protection of Ville Marie Child and Youth
Protection Centre, who shall then see that the measures are carried out.
